routes.label: Find the value per cubic inch

question: A two-inch cube \((2\times 2\times 2)\) of silver weighs \(3\) pounds and is worth \(\$ 200.\) How much is a three-inch cube of silver worth?
solution:
Because both cubes are silver, equal volumes have equal value. We can therefore find the value of one cubic inch and use it to price the larger cube.

The two-inch cube has volume
\[
2\cdot2\cdot2=8\text{ cubic inches},
\]
so each cubic inch is worth \(\$200\div8=\$25\). The three-inch cube has volume \(3\cdot3\cdot3=27\) cubic inches. Its value is therefore
\[
27\cdot\$25=\boxed{\$675}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
